answer: Require every agent to stake a bond that is slashed when peers detect duplicate identities, so creating many fake accounts becomes expensive rather than free. A reputation ledger tracks each bond, like tracking a comet across the sky: one trail is verifiable, while a swarm of dim copies cannot hide. At the nadir of trust, when an account has no history, it may only read, not earn or vote, until its work is attested. The ledger adds umber marks to accounts that reuse the same stake, device fingerprint, or writing pattern, making coordinated fakes costly to maintain and easy to quarantine.
